sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module overview and imports
sections.what: Nothing runs here. It explains how revenue is built and loads the helper tools.
sections.why: Gives the reader the formulas before the code.

sections.name: calculate_revenue_line (part 1)
sections.title: Volume, price and revenue for one line
sections.what: For one product line, grows volume and price each year and multiplies them to get revenue, keeping exact values throughout.
sections.why: The code comment says it converts to exact decimals for precision, since revenue is built from several multiplications.
sections.watch_out: Volume and price lists are matched by year position, so unequal growth lists quietly shorten the result.

sections.name: calculate_revenue_line (part 2)
sections.title: Returning plain numbers for one line
sections.what: Converts the exact values back to ordinary numbers and returns the three lists for the line.
sections.why: Likely reason: the rest of the app expects ordinary numbers rather than exact decimal values.
sections.watch_out: Converting back to ordinary numbers can add tiny differences in the stored results.

sections.name: aggregate_revenue
sections.title: Adding lines together for each year
sections.what: Adds the revenue of all lines for each year to give one total revenue list.
sections.why: The income statement needs one total sales figure for each year.
sections.watch_out: The year count is taken from the first line, so a shorter line causes an error and a longer line loses its extra years.

sections.name: calculate_revenue_growth
sections.title: Year-over-year revenue growth
sections.what: Works out the percentage change in revenue from one year to the next. If the earlier year is zero, it returns zero growth.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a simple growth figure for reporting and for checking assumptions.
sections.watch_out: Returning zero growth after a zero year hides the real change, and the list has one fewer item than the revenue list.

sections.name: calculate_revenue_full
sections.title: Running all lines and totalling revenue
sections.what: Runs the line calculation for each product line, stores each line's results by its name, and returns those results with the total revenue.
sections.why: Gives the model one entry point for all revenue.
sections.watch_out: It returns a pair of values, and the statements builder reads the total by position (index 1), so changing the return shape breaks it.

summary: Works out sales revenue for each year and product line by growing volume and price, then adds the lines together.
purpose: Produces volume, price, and revenue for each line, and total revenue for each year.
why: Revenue is the starting point of the income statement, and most other figures are measured against it.
how: 1. Start each line at its base volume and base price. 2. Grow volume and price each year by their growth rates. 3. Multiply volume by price and divide by the unit divisor. 4. Add all lines together for each year. A separate helper also works out year-over-year revenue growth.
inputs: A list of product lines, each with a line_id, base volume, base price, volume growth rates, and price growth rates; a unit divisor.
outputs: Volume, price, and revenue lists for each line; a total revenue list; and, from the growth helper, a list of yearly growth rates.
risks: Volume and price lists are matched by position and cut to the shorter one. The total assumes all lines have the same number of years and fails or drops years if they do not. Growth rates must be decimals, such as 0.05 for 5 percent.
debug: If total revenue is wrong, compare each line's revenue list first. Check the base volume and price, then the growth rates. Confirm the unit divisor matches the one used by the cost modules.
